parsed_json.explanation: Time: O(n · k log k) where n is the number of elements and k is the average number of enumerable keys per object; sorting the keys dominates per-object work and JSON.stringify is O(k). Space: O(n · k) for the Set storing one canonical JSON string per unique object. Objects that are not plain objects (null, arrays, primitives) are always preserved without deduplication since they have no comparable key/value structure.

label: C-multifile-feature-r0

parsed_json.explanation: Both files are concatenated into one scope, so chooseRoute can call hasCapacity directly; function declarations are hoisted, so call order does not matter. capacity.js validates inputs strictly: active must be a nonnegative integer and limit a positive integer, throwing RangeError otherwise, and returns active < limit. route.js reuses that validation, then routes high-complexity tasks or those with two or more failures to DEEP_LOCAL_WORKER. Otherwise it returns FAST_LOCAL_WORKER when capacity is available and QUEUE when saturated. No cloud fallback is implemented, per the constraint.
